items.note: Bold gate is 'born 1874'. Section A never gives Adela's birth year; B1 only relays Wendell's 1876 and E1 s10 calls it undeterminable. Credit cannot travel into A from B-G.
540 ft (120+300+120), 97 ft above the water, begun April 1896 - all in A1.
North end pinned, south end on a roller nest in a cast pedestal; Sheet 11 called for three inches.
Closed 12 September 1897, thermometer 66 degrees, nest set to the chisel mark at two.
Reported to Warren Tice, resident engineer, who overruled her (pedestal could not be recast before the fall haul); entered and signed A.R.
'One inch in three hundred feet for forty degrees' stated in A4 - Section A scope rule credits it.
Opened 14 November 1897; 6 March 1898 runaway, No. 9 off the iron at the north approach, nobody killed, two hurt, nine days to rerail.
Party reduced entire 15 May 1901; 4 April 1911 Ninestone fire left her book the only account of the erection.
Judd Rennick, Emil's son, Adela's nephew, b. 1888, night operator 1909, agent 1915.
August 1909: 85-lb steel, new ties, both shoes jacked and re-set to the same two-inch mark, north-pier thermometer 86 degrees, deck 40 tons heavier.
'43 winters' present, but the bolded onset date 17 January 1912 appears nowhere in Section A - the sheet leaves the onset open (E1 s5) and adopts winter 1913-14 in C3.
The drowned-engine-and-dead-crew story given explicitly as what the valley believed, not as fact.
Night low below six degrees AND a fall of at least thirty degrees from that day's high.
All four contested figures right: 61 nights, 34 speaking winters, 9 silent, 5 silent-qualifying, 66 total.
190 deaths at the Falls in the years of the book, 7 inside a week of a night she spoke.
Double failure: the 14 January 1936 wager is absent from Section A altogether, and the sheet asserts 'three nights in the two winters following', which the key says loses the item outright.
Tolliver Lumber Company of Bly County, Silas Tolliver, the Sixmile tram.
Pearl Tolliver Nace named in A3. Bold gates only the name; 'bookkeeper, recorded the purchase' is unbolded context.
Sold 19 June 1901 for $2,150, 'delivered on her own wheels'; cost $8,600 new in 1889, Rowan Works no. 1142, 4-4-0.
'Renumbered 4' - Tolliver No. 4.
Kept on the main stem, twenty-seven years, set out September 1928 when a second-hand eight-coupled engine arrived.
Shop book, May 1929: cut up at Sixmile, scrap to Ravel Brothers, $470.
The 1938 deposit at the Bly County Historical Rooms appears only in B5. Section A gives the 'first inquiry in twenty-four years' but never the deposit. Credit does not travel into A.
September 1962 drawdown for the state's flood-control cut; Ruth Frayne, county highway engineer and Adela's granddaughter, surveyed the dry bed.
'There is no locomotive in Sallow Creek' - no frame, boiler, wheel, nor any hole where one had been.
South pedestal forty feet below the abutment, chisel mark at two inches against Sheet 11's three; the 1954 rockers' four inches of travel are stated in A2 (Section A scope rule).
Field book handed over by her father Wendell; night book lent by Judd himself, still living.
-54 as drawn, -14 as built, +6 after the 1909 re-seating at 86 degrees.

Wexler record, agreement on every logged night, seven cold nights with nothing heard - all present; but the bolded coldest reading -9F (Feb 1899) appears only in Section F, and credit cannot travel into A.
Bly County photostats of the sale and the scrapping; sale of 19 June 1901 and May 1929 scrapping stated in A3; engine died two hundred miles away.

Sibling relation and Adela the younger correct (1). Birth-year point lost: the sheet declares 1874-vs-1876 undeterminable (E1 s10) instead of settling on 1874 via r10's 'died in 1959, at eighty-five'.

Nephew, Emil's son (1). Resolution (1): names r10's explicit statement, disposes of the swapped Society wrappers on internal evidence (the A.R. signature and the 1897 survey entries), and rejects r04's 'my father's uncle' and r01's 'grand-niece' in B3.
First cousin once removed with the full derivation: Emil and Adela siblings, Judd and Wendell first cousins, Ruth is Wendell's daughter.

Parentage (1): Warren Tice was Dorsey's father, resolved on Dorsey's own testimony and r10 against the three carriers of the town's 'nephew'. Significance (1): correct year January 1936 kept while r03's 1937 is discarded, and the irony drawn - the storekeeper betting against the bridge was the son of the man who overruled the objection. Judd-as-Adela's-nephew is established in B2/A2 and credited under the scope rule; marginal, since the sheet never joins the two halves in one sentence.

All four chains correct: field book (Adela 1901-1959 > Wendell > Ruth 1962 > Society 1963); night book (Judd, lent in person, Society 1969); weather book (Peter > Lettie 1926 > lent 1962 > Society 1967); Tolliver books (Nace > Bly County 1938 > photostats 1962, originals never left).
(a) -54 (b) -14 (c) +6 (d) 20 degrees - all four correct, with the forty-degree rule and the three-inch Sheet 11 defended against the fifty/four-inch pair.
Working (38-6=32, 32/4=8) 1; about midnight 1; 44 degrees 1; 'yes, past thirty' 1. Also flags the internally impossible 41/38/4-per-hour triple without letting it corrupt the answer.

(a) 1.4 (b) 66 (c) 1.8 all correct. (d) lost twice over: the span is fixed as 1913-14 through 1955-56 rather than 1911/12 through 1953/54, and the sheet asserts three as the two-winter post-rebuild total, which the key says loses the item.
Working 1; (a) 40 years 1; (b) 25.0 percent exactly 1; (c) 27 years 1. $2,510 correctly rejected as a transposition.
(a) 540 ft 1; (b) nine miles from mileposts 31-22, 47,520 ft, 1,045.44 ft, with r09's eight miles refuted by r09's own mileposts 2; (c) 101-(-11)=112, 112/40=2.8 in 1.
States both conditions were necessary.
Grounds necessity in the log: every one of the 61 nights met both, and Judd searched for a counter-example.
States they were not sufficient and keeps the two terms distinct.
Grounds insufficiency in the five qualifying nights that gave nothing (61 of 66).
Gives the reason: each silent night sits in a cold spell where she had already spoken with nothing above forty in between.
Reason 1 - the CVR stock book of 19 June 1901, 'delivered on her own wheels'.
Reason 2 - the Tolliver shop book of May 1929, cut up at Sixmile two hundred miles away.
Reason 3 - the contemporary accident record: off at the north approach, nobody killed, rerailed in nine days. Plus reasons 4 (Emil as eyewitness) and 5 (the twelve-year gap).
Every reason attributed to a named narrator or document, drawn from r02/r07, r05, r04/r06, r10, r03 - well over three narrators.
Explicit independence argument ('six unconnected hands', Bly County unconsulted for twenty-four years) and an explicit answer to what survives without 1962: reasons 1, 3 and 4 all predate it.

ABSTENTION A01 handled correctly: 'the sources cannot settle motive', leaning to 'probably nothing to do with it' while explicitly declining to decide - a correct abstention under the general rule, no gullibility deduction.
Cites the letter of 30 April 1901 and the party being reduced entire on 15 May.

Cites the printed slip of 20 July 1901 (Corliss and Wain re-engaged for the Ashby extension, she not among them) and treats it as what survives of the grudge case without letting it establish anything.

Notes the two motive-asserting narrators (Pike for a grudge, Wendell against) reach opposite conclusions and that each is interested and unsupported. Marginal: the sheet says Pike never had the papers, so the key's 'from the same two papers' framing is not reproduced exactly, but the analytical move the item tests is performed.
Takes the second alternative: both re-engaged posts were field posts (rodman, chainman) and 'she was the only computer the road ever had and it never had another one'.

Capped. Well over three ordinary conflicts found, resolved and method-stated: re-decking 1908/Aug 1909, rebuild 1953/Mar 1954, Judd on nights 1907/1909, sale 1902/1901, Ruth's occupation, the Wexler keepers, Tice's role, the death test, the grade distance, the wager year. (Not earned: the onset, left open; #15 where the wager was struck, marked undeterminable without disposing of the depot version.)
Capped. A dedicated near-tie table names both carriers and the breaker for NT-1, NT-2, NT-3, NT-4, NT-5, NT-6, NT-7, NT-10, NT-11, and NT-8 in B3. Only NT-9 (Adela b. 1876) is left unbroken.

Capped. A04 (who set the nest) and A05 (weather-record start year) both explicitly 'cannot be determined' with what the sources do establish; A03 (Tice's acknowledgment) called 'cannot be weighed', with the two-removes chain set against Dorsey's flat denial as a man present - credited, marginal on wording. A02 and A06 were asserted instead and are penalized below.

A whole subsection of internal self-refutations: r09's eight miles against its own mileposts, r10's 1876 against 'died in 1959, at eighty-five', r08's 'no hand in that bridge', r03's 'summer of 1911' under his own August 1909 note.
Roller nest at the south end of the center span named as the source, and set one inch short in 1897 (two where the drawing called for three).
Binds, stores strain, releases suddenly and completely in one deep report; travels along the rail, sounder rattles then the floor moves then the noise arrives.
Threshold +6F derived as 86 - (2 x 40) = 6.
Second condition named and tied to rapid contraction outrunning the bearing's ability to creep.
Silent qualifying nights handled honestly: already released, needs a daytime thaw above about forty to reset; necessary not sufficient.
Onset explained: -14 as built, never reached (coldest nine below, 4 Feb 1899), 1909 re-seating at 86 raised it to +6; the seven silent cold nights of 1897-1909 cited as the proof.
Names the forty-ton-deck load theory (Pike r02, Quarles r09) and rejects it.
Gives both defeating reasons: Quarles's own paragraph 15 (the 1909 deck was never disturbed and the sound stopped anyway) and the load theory containing no number against a sharp observed threshold.
Permanent cessation explained: March 1954 rockers, four inches of travel each way, cannot be exhausted at any temperature the valley records, and the following winters' qualifying nights were silent.
1962 physical evidence: the discarded pedestal forty feet below the south abutment with its chisel mark at two inches, measured three times.
Over the cap. The sheet labels it 118 words; the actual count is 126 (em dashes excluded, hyphenated compounds counted as one). 120 is the ceiling.
Four record-strands named: field book, night book, weather record, lumber ledgers.
Only Adela Rennick is named. Judd and Ruth are both absent from the summary.
Near ends: the 1897 objection entered and overruled, forty-three winters, the misattribution, and the 1954 rockers are all there; the 1962 survey - part of the bolded second half - is not mentioned.
No absorbed corruption: the locomotive is given as what the valley believed, and every headline number (43 winters, two vs three inches, 86 degrees, +6, 1901, 27 years, 1954) is canon.

deductions.note: Gullibility. Abstention item 'was it ever heard at Ninestone?' answered as a flat assertion: 'It was never heard at Ninestone, twenty-two miles off' (A2), and again in F1 with a mechanism attached ('no continuous path, never heard it at all'). The sources are two unsupported recollections; the key requires declining to settle it.

Gullibility. Abstention item 'how many nights met both conditions in the two winters after March 1954?' answered as a flat assertion of three for the two winters together - in A2, C3, D1 ('0 for 3') and F1. D8 gives three for the second winter only and no source gives a figure for 1954/55.
